_readme: Savings factors for the planner's estimator. pctHeating = share of annual HEATING spend saved, as [low, high] decimals. eras limits which archetypes a measure applies to (empty = all). heatingTypes limits by heating fuel (empty = all). Edit freely — the engine reads this file.
wholeHouseNote: Individual measure savings overlap — they don't simply add. Audit-guided whole-home retrofits in older Ontario homes typically land in the 15–35% range overall.

measures.label: Air sealing
measures.note: Blower-door-guided sealing lands at the high end in leaky homes.

measures.label: Air sealing (targeted)
measures.note: Tighter eras have less to seal — but rim joists and attic penetrations still pay.

measures.label: Attic top-up to R-60
measures.note: Assumes current attic is R-20 or less. HRSP insulation rebates apply on the assessment path.

measures.label: Attic top-up to R-60
measures.note: Smaller gain from R-32 up — still often worth it at these install prices.

measures.label: Wall insulation (drill-and-fill)
measures.note: For empty frame cavities. Solid masonry needs a different (costlier) strategy — get audit guidance first.

measures.label: Basement & rim joist insulation
measures.note: Up to $7,700 of HRSP insulation rebates can apply across attic/wall/basement combined.

measures.label: Window & door upgrades
measures.note: Comfort and noise improve more than bills — sequence after cheaper envelope work. HRSP pays $100/opening.

measures.label: Cold-climate heat pump (replacing electric baseboard)
measures.note: The biggest single bill cut in Ontario. HRSP rebates up to $12,000 for electrically heated homes.

measures.label: Heat pump / hybrid (replacing gas furnace + AC)
measures.note: At current Ontario gas prices the dollar case is modest — the wins are included cooling, comfort, and emissions. A hybrid (heat pump + gas backup) hedges rates. Model it with your auditor.

measures.label: Cold-climate heat pump (replacing oil or propane)
measures.note: Oil-heated homes usually see the fastest paybacks of any fuel switch.

measures.label: Heat pump water heater
measures.note: Savings shown as dollars, not a heating percentage — biggest for electric tanks.

measures.label: Smart thermostat & setbacks
measures.note: Cheapest item on the list — do it regardless.

measures.label: HRV (heat recovery ventilator)
measures.note: Buy it for air quality and condensation control; energy recovery is the bonus.

measures.label: Rooftop solar + battery
measures.note: Assumes a typical 6–8 kW array at Ontario production (~1,100 kWh per kW installed per year). Roof orientation and shading move this a lot.
